title: Mars utility-corridor thermics, piping and resilience audit for OTA-TEC-0091
question: Source-grounded audit of the exact OTA-TEC-0091 Mars Utility Corridor dossier. Assess: (1) what Antarctic, Arctic and permafrost utilidor systems demonstrate as an architectural analogy and which construction details do not transfer directly to Mars; (2) water and wastewater freeze protection, pipe insulation, heat tracing, pumping and pressure-loss constraints under Mars ambient conditions; (3) surface, enclosed, partially buried and buried corridor trade-offs including regolith thermal properties, settlement and maintenance access; (4) safe co-routing while keeping potable water, wastewater, high-power electrical and data systems physically separated; (5) leak detection, segmentation, bypass/ring architectures and how to avoid turning a common corridor into a common-mode single point of failure; (6) whether shared corridors actually reduce construction/inspection burden after containment and redundancy requirements are included; and (7) wording that should stay [H]/[OFFEN]. Do NOT set pipe sizes, heat-trace watts, corridor spacing, build costs, network bonuses or NOXIA balancing values.
why_now: OTA-TEC-0091 is an uncovered mapped infrastructure object and explicitly remains ENTWURF pending Mars-specific thermics/ground conditions and redundancy/common-mode-failure rules.
real_world_anchor: Polar/permafrost utilidors, insulated and heat-traced water/wastewater systems, pipeline thermics, leak isolation and resilient utility-network architecture, interpreted under Mars environmental constraints.
novelty_reason: Covers distribution-network thermics and common-corridor resilience, not the water-extraction process already researched for OTA-TEC-0034.
